course: AWS Certified Generative AI Developer – Professional (AIP-C01)
review_basis: Original R2 slide audit, topic-first lecture grouping on slides 45-50; fresh narration/audio, no five-slide limit.
part_title: Security Architecture Decision Guides and Integrated Review

scenes.title: Identity decision guide
scenes.narration: This slide is a decision tree, so begin with the identity of the caller rather than picking a service name first. An AWS workload such as Lambda, ECS or EC2 should generally assume an IAM role and use temporary credentials. A human workforce member who needs access to multiple AWS accounts should use IAM Identity Center with centrally managed permission sets and federation. A customer using your application needs sign-up and authentication through a user-facing identity system such as a Cognito user pool. If that customer's client must access an AWS service directly, a Cognito identity pool can exchange an authenticated identity for limited, temporary AWS credentials. Contrast that with an IAM user: it represents an individual identity in an AWS account, with possible long-lived credentials, and is usually not the preferred default for workforce sign-in. The diagram distinguishes who authenticates from what resources are authorised. A user-pool token isn't itself an AWS IAM access key, and being signed in never authorises every database record. To make a good architectural choice, name the caller, choose an authentication method, then specify exactly which resources and API actions the resulting identity can use.

scenes.title: Encryption decision guide
scenes.narration: Let's compare the four paths rather than treating encryption as one interchangeable feature. TLS protects information moving over the network: your application and AWS endpoint negotiate a protected session, but authorised endpoints can still see plaintext after decryption. Server-side encryption protects stored objects or database data, with the service managing the encryption operation and supported key controls. Client-side encryption moves that operation into your application before data is uploaded, so the storage provider receives ciphertext; the application must manage decryption and recovery. Envelope encryption adds a scalable key-management pattern: a short-lived data key encrypts content and a KMS key protects the data key. It can support application-side or service-side implementations depending on the design. Follow the comparison rows for plaintext location, key ownership, use cases and operational responsibilities. The key question is not only whether data is encrypted but where plaintext exists and who can obtain the relevant keys. For GenAI, a prompt decrypted before a model invocation becomes plaintext at that inference boundary. Design security across the complete data path, including access policies, transport, memory and storage.

scenes.title: Data protection decision guide
scenes.narration: This slide distinguishes protecting sensitive data from discovering it. Masking hides selected values while preserving useful structure, for instance showing only part of an email address before it reaches a model. Tokenization replaces a sensitive value such as a payment-card number with a token whose mapping lives in a protected vault. Anonymization aims to prevent identification or re-identification, which is much stronger than substituting a user ID; meaningful anonymization must be assessed against combinations of fields and external data. Macie is different: it discovers and classifies sensitive information in S3. It does not automatically transform every document into safe training data. Follow the pipeline along the bottom. First discover sensitive material, then apply an appropriate protection method, then use the protected data in RAG indexing, fine-tuning or inference, and finally review what the model shares. Consider reversibility and purpose. A system that needs to restore the original value may use controlled tokenization; a publicly shared analytic dataset should require stronger anonymization. Keep the mapping vault and any decryption permissions separate from ordinary model access.

scenes.title: Network security decision guide
scenes.narration: Here the architecture presents six different traffic problems. Follow the public request through AWS WAF to the load balancer. WAF examines HTTP and HTTPS requests for web-layer threats; it does not replace user authentication. Security groups then control allowed traffic at an application resource's network interface and automatically allow return traffic for permitted connections. Network ACLs operate at the subnet boundary using stateless, ordered allow-and-deny rules. When private instances need general outbound internet access, a NAT gateway can provide egress without exposing them to unsolicited inbound traffic. When the destination is a supported AWS service such as S3, DynamoDB or Bedrock, a VPC endpoint can keep access on private AWS networking instead. PrivateLink can expose a particular provider or SaaS service to an approved consumer without broad VPC peering. Select the control based on the destination and trust boundary. A gateway doesn't authorise a model call, and an endpoint doesn't grant IAM permissions. Map the packet path, route tables, security rules and identity policies together before approving the design.

scenes.title: Security incident evidence chain
scenes.narration: This slide is a time-ordered investigation, not a list of unrelated security services. Begin at ten oh one, when an IAM event shows a principal assuming an administrative role. Next, WAF records a suspicious SQL injection pattern from a source IP and blocks the web request. A VPC Flow Log later shows a connection involving that source address and a workload, identifying network activity but not the full request content. Macie contributes a sensitive-data finding in an S3 location. Finally, CloudTrail records a GetObject API action under an assumed role. The task for an investigator is to correlate timestamps, principals, source addresses, resource names and request identifiers. Avoid overclaiming causality: a blocked WAF request doesn't prove the same caller successfully reached S3, and a Macie discovery finding does not by itself prove exfiltration. CloudTrail supplies important API evidence, while Flow Logs report network metadata and Macie classifies stored sensitive information. Build a verified timeline, preserve records, scope the affected resources and take proportionate containment action.

scenes.title: Integrated Review
scenes.narration: The module's closing diagram follows a request through seven checkpoints: caller, identity, network, encryption, application, data and monitoring. Start with the caller's legitimate need. Confirm that identity is authenticated and authorised, then that routing and network controls allow only the required communication. Verify TLS and appropriate at-rest encryption, and check that the application validates inputs and enforces business-level permissions. At the data layer, review classification, minimisation and resource access. Finally, confirm that logs, metrics and audit events can support investigation without leaking private content. The decision diamond at the bottom asks whether every critical checkpoint passes. A strong result at one stage does not compensate for an unsafe failure at another. For example, encrypted data is still exposed if a role has excessive read permissions; a private network can still carry an unauthorised request. The result is a repeatable architecture review: trace the real user journey, identify every trust boundary, test both allowed and denied paths, and remediate gaps before declaring the system production ready.
